gaps.sentence: Unless you ___ the form by Friday, your application will not be considered.
gaps.hint: unless means if not, present simple
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if not' and, like if, takes the present simple: submit.

gaps.sentence: If this medicine ___ relief within an hour, call me back.
gaps.explanation: Conditional instructions use the present simple in the if-clause: does not bring.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ a muscle, apply ice at once.
gaps.hint: medical instruction, present simple after if
gaps.explanation: The if-clause of a conditional instruction uses the present simple, never 'will': pull.

gaps.sentence: We will lose the deposit if we ___ the booking now.
gaps.explanation: The result clause carries 'will'; the if-clause stays in the present simple: cancel.

gaps.sentence: If only we ___ the tickets before they sold out!
gaps.explanation: 'If only' plus the past perfect regrets a missed past opportunity: had bought.

gaps.sentence: If only I ___ my umbrella — I am getting soaked!
gaps.hint: present regret about an earlier decision
gaps.explanation: 'If only' plus the past perfect expresses a present regret about a past decision: had brought.

gaps.sentence: Should you ___ any problems, please contact support.
gaps.explanation: 'Should you plus infinitive' is a formal way to say 'If you ...': experience.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ me, I would have helped you move house.
gaps.hint: a missed request in the past
gaps.explanation: An unreal past condition takes the past perfect: had asked.
